raw_text:
Great—let’s lay out a structured 12-week muscle gain program for a 26-year-old recreational lifter who is vegan, using a full gym. The plan will cover periodized training (phases), week-by-week structure, exercise selections, sets/reps, progression, and a plant-based nutrition plan aiming for ~150 g protein/day. I’ll include recovery strategies, practical tips for vegan protein intake, and example meals.

Assumptions and guidelines
- Training frequency: 4 days/week (strength-focused) with optional 5th day active recovery or accessory work. We’ll alternate upper/lower splits for balanced development.
- Progression: linear progression within phases with small weekly increases in load or volume; deload every 4th week.
- Reps and sets: aimed at hypertrophy and strength (8–12 reps for most work in hypertrophy blocks, some lower-rep strength work in later phases).
- Nutrition: target 150 g protein/day from vegan sources, with overall calories matched to a slight surplus for muscle gain (rough baseline: +250–500 kcal/day above maintenance, adjusted as needed). Protein distribution: 3–5 meals with ~30–40 g protein per meal on training days; include protein-rich vegan foods and supplements (e.g., pea/rice blends, soy products, tempeh, seitan, hemp, quinoa, beans, lentils). Consider a whey-like vegan protein blend if tolerated (e.g., pea+rice).
- Recovery: 7–9 hours sleep, daily protein spread, fiber timing around workouts, hydration, microcycle deloads, mobility work.

Phase structure
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Hypertrophy foundation + technique. Higher volume, moderate intensity. Establish consistency, learn lifts, build work capacity.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength and hypertrophy blend. Introduce more compound loading, progress intensity, maintain volume.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Maximal strength + metabolic stress for growth. Higher intensity with lower reps, refined technique, finish with a deload in Week 12 if needed and then a transition into a maintenance/transition plan.

Weekly schedule (4 days)
- Day 1: Upper Body A (bench emphasis)
- Day 2: Lower Body A (quad-dominant)
- Day 3: Rest or light cardio/ mobility
- Day 4: Upper Body B (pull emphasis)
- Day 5: Lower Body B (hip/glute emphasis)
- Day 6-7: Rest or optional accessory
- Optional Day 5 could be swapped with a full-body conditioning session if desired.

Detailed week-by-week plan

Weeks 1–4: Hypertrophy foundation
Goals: technique mastery, 8–12 rep ranges, moderate load, establish protein targets.

Week 1
- Day 1 Upper A
  - Barbell Bench Press 4x8
  - Dumbbell Incline Press 3x10
  - Seated Cable Row 3x10
  - Dumbbell Shoulder Press 3x12
  - Dumbbell Lateral Raise 3x12
  - Triceps Pushdown 3x12
- Day 2 Lower A
  - Back Squat 4x8
  - Romanian Deadlift 3x10
  - Leg Press 3x12
  - Walking Lunges 2x12 per leg
  - Leg Curl 3x12
  - Calf Raise 4x15
- Day 4 Upper B
  - Pull-Ups or Lat Pulldown 4x8–10
  - Barbell Rows 3x10
  - Overhead Press 3x10
  - Cable Face Pulls 3x12
  - Dumbbell Curls 3x12
  - Triceps Dips or Extension 3x12
- Day 5 Lower B
  - Deadlift variation (conventional or trap bar) 3x6–8
  - Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8–10 per leg
  - Hip Thrust 3x10
  - Glute Ham Raise or Leg Curl 3x12
  - Ab work: Plank 3x45–60s

Weeks 2–4 (progression)
- Increase sets by 1–2 on primary lifts or add 2–5% load where form allows.
- Maintain rep ranges 8–12.
- Add slow eccentric emphasis where safe (e.g., 3–4s on the lowering phase) on main lifts.

Key notes
- Prioritize technique on compound lifts; use ROM-friendly ranges to protect joints.
- If any lift causes pain, substitute with a safe alternative (e.g., leg press for squat).

Weeks 5–8: Strength and hypertrophy blend
Goals: increase intensity, preserve hypertrophy, start progressive overload more aggressively.

Week 5
- Day 1 Upper A
  - Barbell Bench Press 4x6–8
  - Dumbbell Flyes 3x10
  - Bent-Over Barbell Rows 4x8
  - Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press 3x8–10
  - Lateral Raises 3x12
  - Cable Triceps Pushdown 3x10–12
- Day 2 Lower A
  - Front Squat or Back Squat 4x6–8
  - Romanian Deadlift 3x8–10
  - Leg Press 3x10–12
  - Walking Lunges 3x12 per leg
  - Leg Curl 3x12
- Day 4 Upper B
  - Weighted Pull-Ups or Lat Pulldown 4x6–8
  - T-Bar Rows 3x8–10
  - Overhead Press 4x6–8
  - Face Pulls 3x12
  - Hammer Curls 3x10–12
  - Dips or Skull Crushers 3x10–12
- Day 5 Lower B
  - Deadlift 3x4–6
  - Hip Thrust 4x6–8
  - Split Squat 3x8–10
  - Glute Ham Raise or Leg Curl 3x10–12
  - Calf Raises 4x12–15

Weeks 6–8 (progression)
- Add 1–2 reps on main sets or +5–10 lbs depending on lift.
- Maintain 6–8 rep ranges on major lifts; 8–12 on accessory.

Weeks 9–12: Max strength emphasis + hypertrophy finisher
Goals: push heavier loads, maintain muscle mass, introduce density work and a deload if needed.

Week 9
- Day 1 Upper A
  - Barbell Bench Press 5x5
  - Incline Dumbbell Press 3x8
  - Barbell Rows or Pendlay Rows 4x6
  - Standing Military Press 4x6
  - Face Pulls 3x12
  - Triceps Pushdowns 3x10
- Day 2 Lower A
  - Back Squat 5x5
  - Romanian Deadlift 3x6–8
  - Leg Press 3x10
  - Lunges 3x8 per leg
  - Leg Curls 3x10
  - Calf Raises 4x12–15
- Day 4 Upper B
  - Pull-Ups/Chin-Ups 5x5–6
  - Barbell Rows 4x6–8
  - Dumbbell Overhead Press 4x6–8
  - Shrugs 3x10
  - Bicep Curls 3x10–12
  - Dips or Skull Crushers 3x8–10
- Day 5 Lower B
  - Deadlift 4x4–6
  - Hip Thrust 4x6–8
  - Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8–10
  - Hamstring Curls 3x10–12
  - Calf Raises 4x12–15

Weeks 10–12 (peak intensity + density)
- Week 10: 5x5 main lifts, maintain accessory
- Week 11: 3–4x4–6 for primary lifts, accessories 3x8–10
- Week 12: Deload or taper depending on client readiness; options:
  - Deload: 3 days total body at 60–70% load, reduced volume
  - Or maintain but reduce volume by 20–30% and keep technique sharp

Optional weekly structure (training session snapshots)
- Upper A: bench press emphasis with upper body pulling emphasis
- Lower A: squat emphasis with deadlift accessory
- Upper B: pulling emphasis with overhead pressing
- Lower B: deadlift emphasis with glute/hamstring accessory

Nutrition plan to hit 150 g protein/day (plant-based)
Total protein target: ~150 g/day. Sample protein sources and distribution:
- Protein per meal target: 30–40 g per main meal
- Typical vegan protein sources (approx protein content per 100 g):
  - Tempeh: 19 g
  - Tofu: 8–15 g (firm)
  - Seitan: 25 g (note gluten sensitivity if any)
  - Lentils: 9 g
  - Chickpeas: 9 g
  - Black beans: 8 g
  - Edamame: 11 g
  - Quinoa: 4 g
  - Chia seeds: 4 g (per 28 g)
  - Hemp seeds: 9 g (per 30 g)
  - Nutrition yeast: 8 g per 16 g
  - Pea protein powder: 20–25 g per scoop
  - Rice protein: ~20 g per scoop
- Sample day (training day):
  - Breakfast: 1 cup cooked oats with 2 tbsp hemp seeds (20 g protein total from seeds) + 1 scoop vegan protein shake (20 g) = ~40 g
  - Snack: 1 cup soy yogurt (6–10 g) + 1 oz almonds (6 g) = ~12–16 g
  - Lunch: Lentil + quinoa bowl with tempeh (tempeh 20 g) = ~30 g
  - Snack: Hummus (2–3 tbsp ~2 g) with whole grain pita (6 g) + protein bar (15–20 g) = ~20 g
  - Dinner: Tofu stir-fry with vegetables and brown rice (tofu 15 g) = ~25 g
  - Post-workout: 1 scoop pea or blend protein shake (20 g)
  - Daily total: ~150 g protein (adjust portions and protein powder to hit target)
- Non-training days: distribute protein evenly across meals to maintain muscle protein synthesis
- Practical tips:
  - Prioritize a protein-rich breakfast to start the day.
  - Use a protein supplement near workouts to boost intake and convenience.
  - Combine legumes with grains to ensure complete amino acid profile.
  - Season with soy sauce, nutritional yeast for B12 enrichment (note B12 is essential; vegan B12 supplement is recommended).
  - Consider B12, D, iodine, calcium, iron, omega-3 (ALA from flax/chia/walnuts; consider algae-based DHA/EPA) supplementation as needed via a dietitian.

Calories and macro targets
- Calorie surplus: Start with +250–350 kcal/day above maintenance and adjust based on weekly weight changes (aim for ~0.25–0.5 kg per week). Weight gain targets vary; adjust as needed.
- Carbohydrates: important for performance; target around 3–5 g/kg/day depending on energy expenditure.
- Fats: roughly 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day.

Recovery and ancillary work
- Sleep: 7–9 hours per night.
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day, more on training days.
- Mobility: 10–15 min post-workout focusing on hips, thoracic spine, shoulders.
- Deload every 4th week (weeks 4, 8, 12 optional) with reduced volume and intensity by ~40–60%.
- Injury prevention: warm-ups with 5–10 minutes light cardio, dynamic stretches, then activation exercises (glute bridges, banded walks).

Measurement and progression tracking
- Baseline: 1-rep max tests aren’t required every week; track 1–2 working sets at target reps with estimated RPE 7–8.
- Weekly: body weight, body measurements (chest, waist, hips, thighs), progress photos every 4 weeks.
- Adjustments: if weight gain stalls (less than ~0.25 kg/week for two consecutive weeks), increase calories by 150–250 kcal/day or adjust training volume slightly.

Notes and customization
- If client has dietary preferences (e.g., avoids soy or gluten), swap protein sources accordingly and adjust plan.
- If menstrual cycle affects energy, fine-tune training loads (lift lighter during fatigue peaks, then push harder in other weeks).
- For strict vegan, ensure B12 supplementation, monitor iron levels (plant-based iron absorption can be improved with vitamin C-rich foods); consider iron status screening with a clinician if fatigue or symptoms arise.

Deliverables you can use with the client
- A 12-week calendar with Week 1–12 sessions aligned to Days 1–5 schedule.
- A weekly nutrition plan with target protein portions and meal ideas to hit ~150 g/day.
- A tracking sheet for weights, reps, and subjective effort (RPE) plus body measurements every 4 weeks.
- A deload protocol at Weeks 4, 8 (and 12 if needed) with reduced volume and intensity.

If you want, I can tailor this further to her current lifts, equipment access, any injuries, preferred training days, and exact daily schedule.
